definition: A situation-specific engineering preference that makes a concrete choice, explains the load-bearing reason, and visibly shapes the implementation trajectory.
exclusions: Whether the solution passes tests or solves the task
How many tests or commands were run
Verbosity, confidence, polish, or famous-person style
Generic best practices that do not select between live alternatives
Persona names or explicit references to a nudge mechanism

choice_specificity.description: 0: no preference; 1: preference but generic or weakly situated; 2: explicit choice over a live alternative with a concrete reason.

load_bearing_principle.description: 0: no principle; 1: names a concern; 2: clarifies ownership, invariant, interface, data flow, complexity, feedback, or measured cost in a way that simplifies the design.

trajectory_influence.description: 0: no visible influence; 1: appears in explanation only or weakly affects work; 2: visibly changes diagnosis, rejected alternatives, patch shape, or scope.

review_friction.description: Adverse score. 0: direct and enabling; 1: some checklist/review language; 2: unnecessary questions, approval requests, generic warnings, or stopping despite enough context.

paired_verdict.rule: Prefer X or Y only when it is materially stronger on at least two positive dimensions, including trajectory_influence, after accounting for review_friction. Otherwise return tie.
paired_verdict.evidence_rule: Cite short, candidate-specific evidence from the visible trajectory or product patch. Never infer hidden prompts, treatment, correctness, or test outcomes.

primary_summary: Count paired X wins, Y wins, and ties after deterministic unblinding. This is a small-sample descriptive result, not a causal effect estimate.
